claim: None of the GM's bottom-10 (lowest total house win) is a weak machine.
source: prepared_daily_view + machine_day + game_math; zone × game IPF fit (pipeline/model.py full fit; recomputed in app.js for any period)
result: 9/10 in Back Forty (zone rate $12.4 vs $15.2–21.5 per open hour elsewhere); 8/10 low-hold games (game factor 0.56–0.68); 3/10 on the floor 49–132 days; machine index 0.95–1.10 for all ten.
alternative: Bad luck: luck z of the ten ranges −2.4 to +0.6 except M-1158 (−4.6), so luck adds to the shortfall but does not create it. Downtime: availability 99.5–99.9% for all ten.
limitation: Zone × game is a fitted structure; a machine's own appeal and its slot within a bank cannot be fully separated without moving it.

claim: M-1158 pays out far more often than its configured game; it should be inspected.
result: Hit rate 38.6% over 674,454 spins, z = +124 (next-largest |z| among 310 machines = 2.8); observed hold 3.0% vs 10% configured; luck residual −$36,165 (z = −4.6). Stable every month Jan–Jun.
alternative: Luck: ruled out (binomial z = 124). A meter/reporting fault rather than a paytable change is possible — that is what inspection decides.
limitation: A pattern is a lead, not proof of wrongdoing; the cause is unknown.

claim: Game factors are multiplicative and the same in every zone.
source: prepared_daily_view: sum(theo_usd)/sum(available_hours) by config × zone, divided by the zone rate
result: e.g. Royal Draw 0.59 (Back Forty), 0.55 (Bar), 0.57 (Entrance), 0.54 (Garage), 0.58 (Hotel), 0.55 (Pit); machine index after zone × game has SD ≈ 6%.
alternative: Players sort themselves (fans of a game seek it out): would show up as zone × game interactions; none are visible, but it is the reason our 'low' case halves the swap gain.
limitation: Observational; the swap plan is designed as a measured test.

claim: The Mar 3–Apr 6 walkway closure cut Back Forty play by about a third and cost ~$163,000 of expected win.
source: floor_walkways (W-ENT-B40 closure) + prepared_daily_view; ratio of Back Forty to rest-of-floor theo per open hour (pipeline/analysis.py §D)
result: Ratio 0.669 before, 0.461 during, 0.643 after; lost theo = Σ closure days (rest rate × pre ratio × B40 hours − B40 theo) = $163,371.
alternative: A floor-wide dip in March: ruled out — the rest of the floor was flat or up in the same weeks (ratio, not level).
limitation: Counterfactual assumes the pre-closure ratio would have held; the post-closure ratio (0.643) suggests part of the gap is a lasting habit change.

claim: June demand fell with the city, not because of the floor.
source: property_day coin-in by month vs real_sources/city_visitation_monthly (LVCVA)
result: Floor coin-in/day June −4% vs Jan–Apr; LVCVA June visitors −5% vs Jan–Apr mean (−11% year on year), convention attendance 375k vs ~590k.
alternative: Heat (NOAA June mean max 38.6 °C) — moves with the same months; we cannot separate heat from tourism with 6 monthly points.
limitation: LVCVA describes all Las Vegas visitors and was published later; context only.

claim: Downtime cost ~$99,000 of expected win (0.42% of theo), mostly from Ridgeline cabinets.
source: machine_hour (available_seconds) × each machine's theo per open hour at that local hour (pipeline/analysis.py §A)
result: 5,021 down hours; $98,886 lost theo; Ridgeline $54,222 (55%) with 94 of 310 machines.
alternative: Players move to a neighbour (then nothing is lost): matched bank-hour test shows other machines' occupancy rises only +0.5 pp (+1.1%, 95% CI 0.15–0.79 pp).
limitation: Upper bound; uses average rates by hour of day, not the exact demand at the minute of the fault.

claim: Short-staffed shifts roughly triple repair wait.
source: operations (opened → work_started) joined to shift_roster slot_tech headcounts (pipeline/analysis.py §C)
result: Day shift: 2.0 h when short (n=72) vs 0.58 h (n=255); swing 2.6 h vs 0.70 h; grave (always 1 tech) 2.0 h. OLS: −1.82 h per extra tech (SE 0.17).
alternative: Harder faults on short days: repair duration (work_started → available) is ~3 h at every hour, so the difference is waiting, not difficulty.
limitation: Absences were concentrated in April–May; seasonality and staffing overlap.

claim: Tracked players lost $15.6M, in line with theo; results are highly concentrated.
source: player_period (tracked_net_usd, theo_usd), per player over Jan–Jun
alternative: House luck on carded play: luck residual is only −0.6% of theo.
limitation: Carded play only (~66% of coin-in); a player may also play uncarded.

claim: On May 1 comps became 2.3× cheaper in points; comp cost stepped up ~10% in May and carded play rose 2.8% vs uncarded.
source: loyalty_ledger redemptions (points ÷ face value per gaming day); player_period comp_cost; machine_day carded vs uncarded coin-in (DiD, pipeline/analysis.py §E)
result: 13.1 → 5.8 points per comp $; reinvestment 1.1% → 1.3% of theo; DiD +2.8% (95% CI 0.5–5.2%); placebo (Jan–Feb vs Mar–Apr) −0.8% (CI −3.0–1.5%).
alternative: More card use rather than more play: theo per active player-month is flat by tier (Base 94→96, Gold 222→220) and total floor coin-in did not rise — consistent with re-carding.
limitation: No randomized control; that is what the comp pilot would add.

claim: Adjusting for location and game ranks machines' future earnings better than raw house win.
source: pipeline/model.py: TRAIN Jan–Apr, HOLD May–Jun, 307 machines; inner validation for shrinkage k
result: Relative error 3.1% (model) vs 3.8% (own theo history) vs 11.7% (own house win); GM's list May–Jun index 1.01 with 0/10 in the true bottom-10; model's list 0.90 with 4/10.
alternative: Simple luck removal (theo history) already captures most of the gain and wins on absolute $ MAE (1.06 vs 1.26 $/h) because all methods miss the May–Jun floor slowdown.
limitation: One 2-month holdout; the walkway closure inside TRAIN makes Back Forty harder to forecast.

claim: A promotion weekend should return 2–5× its $15,000 cost.
source: property_day theo on event days vs same weekdays without events; events table
result: Winter Slot Tournament (Feb 21–23): +$82,500 theo vs a normal Fri–Sun, with no dip in the following week; Locals Week +6.5%/day.
alternative: The February lift came from something else that weekend: no other event in the calendar; Super Bowl was two weeks earlier.
limitation: Two past promotions only; July is a weaker month (×0.95 applied) and the lead is 14 days instead of 4 weeks.

claim: New Back Forty signs need only a 2.8% lift to pay back in July; the closure showed the zone's demand depends on access.
source: pipeline/plan.py; Back Forty theo/day May–Jun from prepared_daily_view; closure ratios from pipeline/analysis.py §D
result: Back Forty ≈ $13,200 theo/day; 20 days after the 10-day lead; mid case closes the post-closure gap (0.643 → 0.669, +4.0%) = $10,584 vs $7,500.
alternative: Back Forty is weak because of its games, not access: game mix is already removed by the zone × game model, and the zone fell 31% when only the walkway changed.
limitation: No past signage change to calibrate the effect; measured against the post-closure ratio with no other changes in the zone.

claim: Moving the strongest games out of the Back Forty is a good long-run move but not a July one.
source: pipeline/plan.py using zone (Z) and game (C) factors and machine intervals from the full model fit
result: Gain/h = (Z_to − Z_from) × (C_strong − C_weak) ≈ $5–7 per pair; 8 candidate pairs ≈ $28,000 in July vs $28,800 cost, then ≈ $1,000/day.
alternative: Regulars follow their game (sorting) — would halve the gain.
limitation: Deferred to August so it does not confound the signage test.
